title: N-Body Gravitational Simulation
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D N-body gravitational simulation using Three.js. The entire application must be in a single HTML file.

## Three.js Import
Use this importmap in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x050510).
- PerspectiveCamera at (0, 40, 80), looking at origin.
- OrbitControls enabled.
- Ambient light (0x222244) and a point light (0xffffff, intensity 2.0) at origin.

## Gravitational System
- Start with 5 bodies. Each body is a sphere mesh.
- Gravitational constant G = 100 (scaled for visual effect).
- Each body has: mass (random 1-10), position (random within [-20,20]^3), velocity (random within [-2,2]^3).
- Body radius = 0.3 * mass^(1/3).
- Color each body by mass using HSL: hue = mass/10, saturation 0.8, lightness 0.6.
- Use Velocity Verlet integration for gravitational acceleration: a_i = sum over j≠i of G * m_j * (r_j - r_i) / |r_j - r_i|^3. Use softening epsilon = 0.5 to avoid singularity.
- When two bodies come within the sum of their radii, they merge: new mass = m1 + m2, new velocity = momentum-conserving (m1*v1 + m2*v2)/(m1+m2), new position = center of mass.

## Trail Visualization
- Each body leaves a fading trail (last 100 positions) rendered as a line with decreasing opacity.

## Controls
- Press Space to toggle pause/play (start playing).
- Press 'A' to add a new body at random position (max 20 bodies).
- Press 'C' to clear all trails.
- Slider (id='slider-G', range 10 to 500, step 10, default 100) to adjust G.
- Slider (id='slider-dt', range 0.001 to 0.05, step 0.001, default 0.01) to adjust timestep.

## HUD (id='hud')
- Body count (id='hud-bodies')
- Total mass (id='hud-mass'): sum of all masses, 1 decimal
- Total energy (id='hud-energy'): kinetic + potential, 1 decimal
- Merge count (id='hud-merges'): number of merges that have occurred
- Paused status (id='hud-paused'): 'Running' or 'Paused'
- G value (id='hud-G')

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
- `bodyCount`: number
- `totalMass`: number (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `totalEnergy`: number (KE + PE, rounded to 2 decimals)
- `kineticEnergy`: number (rounded to 2 decimals)
- `potentialEnergy`: number (rounded to 2 decimals)
- `mergeCount`: number
- `isPaused`: boolean
- `G`: number (current gravitational constant)
- `dt`: number (current timestep)
- `maxSpeed`: number (fastest body speed, rounded to 2 decimals)
- `centerOfMass`: {x, y, z} (rounded to 2 decimals)
- `frameCount`: number
- `bodiesValid`: boolean (true if no body has NaN position or velocity)

Ensure the animation loop updates __3D_STATE__ every frame before rendering.
physics_constraints: Total mass must be conserved across merges. Momentum must be conserved during merges (within 1% tolerance). No NaN in any body position or velocity. Body count must decrease by 1 per merge. Softening must prevent infinite forces. Total energy should be approximately conserved (within 10% drift over 1000 frames for reasonable dt).
